Small improvements to finding your way around: you can always see where you're searching, recent files are one click away, and `.pst` files open from the Finder.

## What's new

- **Clearer search.** The search bar now says exactly where it looks, using the real names: the selected folder (for example *Inbox*), all folders of that file (for example *archive-2009.pst*), or — when you have more than one file open — all open files. Under the title you can see where the results come from.
- **Search a whole file.** New option to search every folder of one file without also searching your other open files.
- **Recent files in the toolbar.** The **+** button still opens a file right away; click its arrow to pick one of the files you opened before, just like on the welcome screen. They're also under **File → Open Recent**.
- **Open from the Finder.** PST Viewer now appears under **Open With** for `.pst` and `.ost` files, and opens them with a double-click when no other app (such as Outlook) is set up for them.

## Install

Already using PST Viewer? It will offer this update by itself, or choose **PST Viewer → Check for Updates…**.

New users:

1. Download **PST-Viewer.zip** below.
2. Double-click the zip file in your Downloads folder.
3. Drag **PST Viewer** to your Applications folder and open it.

The app is signed and checked by Apple, so it opens with a double-click. It needs macOS 13 Ventura or later and runs on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

More help: https://mukreb.github.io/mac-pst-viewer/
